proved_step: LEMMA B (unit-clause pinning = contraction, restricted form without auxiliary variables). Let the instance be c_i=(a_i,b_i), i in [m], and fix a unit constraint u with a_u = e_j, b_u = c (x_j = c). Let M be the binary matroid on {v_i : i != u} plus e, and let M/U be the contraction by U = v_u. Substituting x_j = c gives the system c'_i = (a'_i, b'_i) on n-1 variables, with a'_i = a_i restricted to coordinates != j and b'_i = b_i + a_{ij} c. Then the MUS clutter of the substituted system equals the port of M/U at e (as subsets of [m] minus u). Proof: phi(a,b) = (a restricted to coordinates != j, b + a_j c) is GF(2)-linear with kernel span{U}, since phi(e_j,c)=0 and phi(a,b)=0 forces a=t e_j, b=t c. Hence r_{M/U}(X) = r(X cup U) - r(U) = rank of phi(X), so M/U is the binary matroid of phi(v_i) plus phi(e) = e'. Lemma A applied to the substituted system finishes the proof. Hence the MUS clutter of the restriction x_j=c is the port of a minor (a contraction) of the original matroid, so port-preservation holds for unit-clause gadgets without auxiliary variables.

evidence: Reviewed by R1181 (different session). Substitution x_j=c maps a.x=b to a'.x'=b+a_j c, i.e. exactly phi. Target e=(0,1) is fixed by phi, so the inconsistency target is preserved. Contraction identity r_{M/U}(X)=r(X u U)-r(U) with r(U)=1 gives rank(phi(X)) as required. proved_step: LEMMA C (private-auxiliary gadgets, affine GF(2) case). Setting: original system with constraints c_i=(a_i,b_i), i in [m], H_i = {x in GF(2)^n : a_i.x=b_i}. For each i take a gadget E_i = a finite set of affine equations over (x, z_i), where z_i are auxiliaries PRIVATE to i (disjoint across i), such that proj_x sol(E_i) = H_i. Gadget system G = disjoint union of E_i, each equation owned by i. Claims: (i) G consistent iff original consistent; more generally for any owner set P, G|_P consistent iff original restricted to P consistent. (ii) For any S in G, let S_i = S cap E_i and P_i = proj_x sol(S_i). Then S is consistent iff no S_i is internally inconsistent and the intersection of the P_i is nonempty (private aux => lifts are independent). (iii) If a_i != 0 or b_i = 0 then P_i in {H_i, whole space, empty}, since an affine subspace containing a hyperplane is the hyperplane or everything. Internal inconsistency of S_i forces E_i inconsistent, i.e. a_i=0, b_i=1. (iv) Pushforward: if S is an MUS of G and no S_i is internally inconsistent, the owner set Q={i: P_i = H_i} is an original MUS. Proof: Q is inconsistent since the intersection of H_i over Q is empty. If Q' is a proper inconsistent subset of Q, pick j in Q minus Q'; deleting S_j makes the remaining intersection a subset of the intersection over Q', hence empty, so S is not minimal. Also owners with P_i = whole contribute no equations to an MUS, so S = union of S_j over j in Q. (v) Every original MUS M is realized: for each j in M choose a minimal T_j in E_j with proj = H_j; then union T_j is an MUS of G with owner set M. Scope: all gadget auxiliaries private to one constraint, affine (GF(2)-linear) gadgets only. Shared auxiliaries across constraints are NOT covered; G0001 stays open for that case. Lemma C does not claim anything about general Post-lattice languages.

Hand-checked counterexample on domain {0,1,2,3} with one private aux bit per gadget (relations as bitmasks over 8 values, projected by p&3): H0={0,2,3} from E0=[149,133], H1={1} from E1=[26,99], H2={1,3} from E2=[138]. The G-MUS S uses one equation per gadget: P0=H0, P1=proj([99])={0,1,2} strictly containing H1, P2=H2. The intersection of all P_i is empty and every single deletion leaves it nonempty, so S is a G-MUS with no internally inconsistent part. The filtered owner set Q={0,2} has H0∩H2={3} nonempty, so Q is consistent and cannot be an original MUS. Mechanism: the projection of a SUBSET of a gadget always contains H_i; the affine proof uses (iii) (a hyperplane-containing subspace is H_i or the whole space), which fails for general relations. proved_step: LEMMA R (repaired owner pushforward and realization for PRIVATE gadgets, arbitrary finite relations, scope limited to hypothesis R). Setting: constraints i in [m] with H_i a subset of X (x-domain); gadget E_i = finite set of relations over (x, z_i), z_i private to i, with pi(E_i) = H_i, where pi = projection to x. Consistent subsets T of E_i have pi(T) a subset of X. HYPOTHESIS R_i: every consistent T subset of E_i has pi(T) in {H_i, X}. Claim (a): if S is a minimal inconsistent subset of G = union of E_i and no S_i is internally inconsistent, then Q = {i : pi(S_i) = H_i} is an original MUS and S = union of S_j over j in Q. Claim (b): for every original MUS M there is a G-MUS with owner set M. Proof of (a): pi(S_i) contains H_i since S_i is a subset of E_i; by R_i, pi(S_i) is H_i or X. Private auxiliaries are disjoint, so a set is consistent iff the intersection of the owner projections is nonempty, hence the intersection over owners equals the intersection over Q of H_i. S inconsistent gives empty intersection over Q, so Q is nonempty and inconsistent. Owners outside Q have projection X and can be dropped without losing inconsistency, so minimality gives S = union over Q of S_j. For j in Q and e in S_j: S minus e is consistent, its owner-j projection is nonempty (else S minus e is internally inconsistent, contradicting minimality), so it is H_j or X by R_j. If it were H_j, the intersection would be the intersection over Q of H_i, which is empty, contradicting consistency. So it is X, giving intersection over Q minus j of H_i nonempty. Every proper subset of Q lies in some Q minus j, and consistency is monotone, so Q is minimal. Proof of (b): for j in M choose T_j minimal among subsets of E_j with pi(T_j) = H_j (H_j nonempty, so such T_j exists). Let S = union of T_j. Its owner projections are H_j, so S is inconsistent. For e in T_j, T_j minus e has nonempty projection set containing H_j and not equal to H_j by minimality, so it is X by R_j; then S minus e is consistent exactly when the intersection over M minus j of H_i is nonempty, which holds by minimality of M. So S is a G-MUS with owner set M. Remark (checked by hand): if H_i is a hyperplane of GF(2)^n (a single affine equation, the affine case), R_i holds automatically, since the only affine subspaces containing a hyperplane are the hyperplane and the whole space. This recovers S0003 (iii) for affine gadgets. Non-affine R fails on the H = {1} gadget example of cm-c792ee2f14a14a34. Scope: private auxiliaries; relations satisfying R for every constraint; does NOT claim R holds for the gadgets a Post-lattice pp-definition produces. Gap left open: which target relations admit R-gadgets (equivalently H_i is a coatom of the lattice of sub-projections of consistent subsets of E_i).

(iii) holds because an affine subspace containing a hyperplane is that hyperplane or the whole space. Hand review of LEMMA R, parts (a)-(b), under hypothesis R_i (every consistent T in E_i projects to H_i or X). (a): for e in S_j, S minus e is consistent, so its owner-j projection is nonempty. By R_j it is H_j or X. If it were H_j, the intersection over Q would be empty, contradicting consistency. So it is X, and the intersection over Q minus j is nonempty, which gives minimality of Q. (b): T_j is consistent (projection H_j is nonempty), so T_j minus e is consistent and its projection is X by R_j and minimality. Then S minus e is consistent exactly when the intersection over M minus j is nonempty, which holds by minimality of M. Remark: for affine (hyperplane) H_i, R_i holds automatically, consistent with S0003. Finite check: cm-b0d39cea246e4f59 found 0 R-violations on affine gadgets (150 trials). Scope: the proof is correct for relations satisfying R_i; the lemma does NOT establish that Post-lattice pp-gadgets satisfy R_i. proved_step: LEMMA R-suff (sufficient condition for hypothesis R_i of S0009). Setting: finite X (x-domain) and Z; relations are subsets of X x Z, with pi the projection to X. Let E = {E_1,...,E_k}, k >= 1, with H = pi(intersection of all E_i) nonempty. CONDITION COND: for k >= 2 and every j, pi(intersection of E_i over i != j) = X. Claim: under COND, every nonempty T subset of E with intersection of T nonempty has pi(intersection of T) in {H, X}, i.e. hypothesis R holds for E. Proof: if T = E, the projection is H by definition. If T is a proper nonempty subset, pick j with E_j not in T. Then T is contained in E minus {E_j}, so intersection of T contains intersection of (E minus {E_j}) as sets of points. Projection is monotone, and the smaller intersection projects onto X by COND, so pi(intersection of T) = X. For k = 1 the only nonempty T is E. QED. Corollary: LEMMA R (S0009) applies to every private gadget family satisfying COND. Scope: COND is sufficient, not necessary (cond_fails_but_R_holds = 624 in the host record). It says nothing about which Post-lattice pp-gadgets satisfy COND, and it does not touch shared auxiliaries (G0001 stays open).

lemma: REPAIR of the port elimination axiom (S0003 counterexample). Let M be a binary matroid, e a non-loop, C1, C2 circuits containing e, f in C1 and C2, f != e, X = C1 u C2. Then some D = C3 - e with C3 a circuit containing e and C3 inside X - f exists iff e lies in a circuit of M|X \ f. Proof: a port member inside (A u B) - f is a circuit C3 through e with C3 inside X - f, i.e. a circuit of M|X \ f through e; the converse reads the same argument backwards. Consequence: the graphic counterexample is the case where e is a coloop of M|X \ f.

proved_step: LEMMA C' (repair of S0003; affine GF(2) gadgets, private auxiliaries, every single constraint consistent i.e. H_i nonempty, so H_i is X or a hyperplane). Setup: E_i affine over (x, z_i), z_i private, proj_x sol(E_i) = H_i. Claim (a): every subset S_i of E_i has P_i = proj_x sol(S_i) in {H_i, X}. Proof: E_i is consistent (H_i nonempty), and any subset of a consistent affine system is consistent, so P_i is a nonempty affine subspace; it contains H_i because fewer equations give a superset of solutions; an affine subspace containing a hyperplane is that hyperplane or X (dimension count); if H_i = X the claim is trivial. Claim (b): for any S in G, S is consistent iff the intersection of the P_i is nonempty (private auxiliaries let each z_i be chosen independently given x). Claim (c): if S is a minimal inconsistent subset of G, then Q = {i : P_i = H_i} is an original MUS and S = union of S_j over j in Q. Proof: the intersection over Q of H_i is empty; owners with P_i = X can be dropped without losing inconsistency, so minimality forces S = union over Q of S_j; if a proper subset Q' of Q were inconsistent, dropping some j in Q minus Q' from S would leave an inconsistent set, contradicting minimality. Claim (d): every original MUS M of the affine system is realized as the owner set of a G-MUS (step (b) of S0009, now with R automatic). Scope: all H_i nonempty (no constraint equal to 0=1). The case with a constraint 0=1 is excluded; there the original MUS is that singleton and is handled separately. Lemma C' does not cover shared auxiliaries, so G0001 stays open. Relation to S0003: the counterexample in cm-43211365d84f4ae3 uses H_2 = empty, which this lemma excludes.

lemma: For a gadget system G where each gadget i is defined by the affine relation z_i = g_i·x + h_i (mod 2) with projection onto X = {x | a_i·x = b_i}, let Q ⊆ [m] be any subset such that H_Q = ⋂_{i∈Q} H_i ≠ ∅. If for every i∈Q and every x∈H_Q the values g_i·x + h_i are constant (i.e., there exists c_Q ∈ {0,1} with g_i·x + h_i = c_Q for all i∈Q and all x∈H_Q), then the family of minimal inconsistent subsets (MUS) of G equals the family of minimal inconsistent subsets of the original constraint system {a_i·x = b_i}_{i∈[m]}, so the MUS clutter of G equals the MUS clutter of the original system.
evidence: the constant-value condition on gadget functions on H_Q guarantees that the pushforward of any inconsistent subset corresponds to an original MUS, establishing the equivalence of MUS families.

lemma: SPECIAL CASE OF G0001 (shared auxiliaries). Author model: claude-haiku-5-5, so no SURVIVED_REVIEW is possible from this session; a reviewer from another model family is needed. Setting: x in {0,1}^n; gadgets E_i with projections H_i = proj_x(sol(E_i)); each E_i has private auxiliaries (pairwise disjoint across i) and shared auxiliaries Z_i. Hypotheses: (FUNC) for each i and each x in H_i, the Z_i-values of any solution of E_i over x are unique; write f_i(x). (AGREE) for all i, j and x in H_i intersect H_j, f_i(x) and f_j(x) agree on Z_i intersect Z_j. Claim: for every owner set P, G|_P (the union of E_i for i in P) is consistent iff the intersection of H_i over i in P is nonempty. Proof. Soundness (any shared auxiliaries): a solution (x,z) of G|_P gives x in H_i for every i in P, so x lies in the intersection. Completeness: take x in the intersection; define Z-values by f_i(x), well defined on all of Z by AGREE; for each i take a private witness of E_i at x (private sets are disjoint, so witnesses combine); by FUNC the Z_i-values of that witness equal f_i(x), so each E_i is satisfied; hence G|_P is consistent. Scope: covers shared auxiliaries that are functions of x in each gadget (Tseitin-style definitions, XOR chains). Does NOT close G0001 for general shared auxiliaries, where FUNC fails. Sanity check against cm-cbb126d3f0404136: H1 and H2 meet at (0,1), but E1 forces z=0 and E2 forces z=1 there, so AGREE fails, consistent with the lemma. Closes: none (special case only; G0001 stays open).

proved_step: Decoupling lemma for a shared existential bit. Setting: finite X; gadgets G_i subset of X x {0,1}; owner projection C_i = {x : exists z, (x,z) in G_i}; for T a set of gadget indices, shared(T) = {x : exists z, for all i in T, (x,z) in G_i} and owner(T) = intersection over i in T of C_i. Hypothesis (forced constants): for each i there is c_i in {0,1} with (x,z) in G_i implies z = c_i. Claim: if all c_i with i in T are equal to c, then shared(T) = owner(T); otherwise shared(T) is empty. Proof: if all c_i = c on T, then (x,z) in G_i forces z = c, so shared(T) = {x : (x,c) in G_i for all i in T}; and (x,c) in G_i iff x in C_i, because z is forced to c whenever x is in C_i. Hence shared(T) = owner(T). If c_i differ on T, no single z satisfies all gadgets in T, so shared(T) is empty. Scope: this is exact only for forced-constant gadgets, where the shared bit is already a constant and the formalization reduces to private gadgets with fixed values. It does NOT close G0001, which concerns shared bits not forced to a constant. Refutation of the determined-z repair (z = f_i(x) on each gadget): X = {x0,x1}, G_1 = {(x,z): z = [x = x1]}, G_2 = {(x,z): z = [x = x0]}, both with x-domain {x0,x1}. Owner: C_1 and C_2 both equal {x0,x1}, so owner({1,2}) is nonempty. Shared: z would need [x=x1] = [x=x0] for some x, which never holds, so shared({1,2}) is empty. Thus z is determined by x on each gadget, yet the shared formalization is spuriously unsat for a satisfiable owner pair.

proved_step: LEMMA P (private pp-gadgets preserve the MUS clutter). Setting: Boolean relations over a finite language Gamma; instance I = (X, (C_i)_{i in [m]}) with C_i = (R_i, u_i), u_i a tuple of variables from X. Assume each R_i has a pp-definition R_i(y) iff exists z phi_i(y, z), phi_i a conjunction of Gamma-constraints. Gadget G(I): fresh variables Z_1..Z_m, pairwise disjoint and disjoint from X; block i is phi_i(u_i, Z_i). Claim: for all S subset of [m], Sat(G(I)_S) iff Sat(I_S), where G(I)_S and I_S are the sub-instances on blocks/constraints in S. Consequently the minimal-unsatisfiable index sets coincide (MUS clutter preserved exactly). PROOF. (=>) Let a satisfy all blocks i in S. Restricting to X, for each i in S the tuple a|u_i satisfies exists z phi_i(., z), i.e. a|u_i in R_i, so a|X satisfies I_S. (<=) Let x satisfy I_S. For each i in S, x|u_i in R_i, so there is a witness w_i with phi_i(x|u_i, w_i). Set a = x on X and a = w_i on Z_i. Block i depends only on u_i and Z_i, and the Z_i are disjoint, so a satisfies every block in S. Hence Sat(G(I)_S). Both directions use only the pp-definition and disjointness; no restriction on Gamma, arity or m. Minimality of an index set is defined from the predicate Sat alone, so the MUS clutters agree. NON-TRIVIAL CONSEQUENCE / NECESSITY OF PRIVACY: with shared auxiliary z, the gadget system satisfies Sat(shared_S) implies Sat(I_S) (projection), so unsat(I_S) implies unsat(shared_S), but not conversely. Counterexample: R_A = {x: x=0} with gadget exists z (x=z and z=0); R_B = {y: y=1} with gadget exists z (y=z and z=1). I_{A,B} is satisfiable (x=0, y=1), while the shared gadget forces z=0 and z=1, so {A,B} becomes a spurious MUS. Scope: exact for private gadgets (the form used by pp-reductions of CSP instances, which substitute a fresh copy of a fixed gadget per constraint). Open: the matroid-port statement for the full dichotomy (Q-7dba34f7a0), and whether every pp-definition used in a reduction can be made private without changing the instance family. Status: CLAIMED until reviewed by a different model family. Relates to S0003 (its owner-set claim is the affine special case of this lemma).

statement: AFFINE CODIM-1 RECORD. Let n>=1, a in GF(2)^n nonzero, b in GF(2), H = {x : a.x = b}. Let E be a finite set of affine equations over (x, z), z = private auxiliaries (any number, any tuple), such that pi(sol E) = H where pi = projection to x and sol E is nonempty. Then for every subset T of E with sol T nonempty, pi(sol T) is H or the whole space GF(2)^n.
proof: (1) sol E is a subset of sol T, so pi(sol E) = H is a subset of pi(sol T). (2) Projection of a nonempty affine subspace of GF(2)^(n+|z|) under a linear map is an affine subspace of GF(2)^n; sol T is affine (solution set of a linear system) so pi(sol T) is affine. (3) H is an affine hyperplane (dimension n-1). Any affine subspace A with H subset of A has dim(A) in {n-1, n}; if dim n-1 then A = H, if dim n then A = whole space. Hence pi(T) in {H, X}. Q.E.D. Consequence: hypothesis R (of Lemma R, S0009) holds automatically for every affine private gadget whose target is an affine hyperplane; so Lemma R applies to all affine codim-1 targets without any check. Scope: GF(2)-affine gadgets, codimension-1 targets only; for codim >= 2 the argument gives only H subset pi(T), not R. Relation to S0003 (iii): this is the same fact, stated for R and with the nonvacuity-free condition.

statement: LEMMA R-sound and LEMMA U (shared auxiliaries allowed). Setting: targets H_i = pi(sol E_i) nonempty, pi = projection to x, E_i finite affine systems over (x,z), z may be shared. (a) If the intersection of H_i over Q is empty, then the union over Q of E_i is inconsistent. (b) If there is Z(x) such that for every i and every x in H_i the fibre {z : (x,z) in sol E_i} equals Z(x), then the union over Q is consistent iff the intersection of H_i over Q is nonempty. Proofs: (a) any solution (x,z) gives x in every H_i, hence in the empty intersection. (b) for x in the intersection pick z in Z(x) (nonempty as x is in H_i); (x,z) satisfies every E_i in Q. Scope: consistency of full owner sets only. Does NOT give the MUS pushforward of S0009(a), which needs consistency of subsets S_i, and subsets can shrink the z-fibre. G0001 stays open.
